blocks.text: Millions in India celebrate Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights – in pictures
The spiritual triumph of ‘light over darkness’ is celebrated during Diwali, which people mark by lighting traditional lamps, decorating homes and gathering with family and friends
A child after lighting firecrackers in Hyderabad on Sunday as millions of people across India celebrate Diwali, the five-day Hindu festival of lights. Photograph: Mahesh Kumar A/AP
Mon 9 Nov 2026 00.42 ESTLast modified on Mon 9 Nov 2026 01.50 EST
People explode firecrackers on roadsides in New Delhi as air pollution remains high in the Indian capital. Photograph: Yanni Rawat/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

A student from a Hindu religious school lights earthen lamps in front of Mani Mandir – commemorating Lord Rama’s return to his kingdom, Ayodhya, after a 14-year exile – in Varanasi. Photograph: Niharika Kulkarni/AFP/Getty Images
Hindu devotees perform rituals, decorating floors with rangoli designs, in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir.Photograph: Faisal Bashir/SOPA Images/Shutterstock

People burst firecrackers outside residential homes in New Delhi. India’s supreme court allowed the sale of certified green firecrackers, permitting their use only during certain hours throughout Diwali. Photograph: Yanni Rawat/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock
Devotees and families with sparklers and firecrackers during Kali Puja, which is observed in West Bengal on the night of Diwali, in Kolkata.Photograph: Sudipta Das/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

People celebrate Diwali in New Delhi. A complete ban on firecrackers is restored from 9 November as authorities seek to curb air pollution in the capital. Photograph: Yanni Rawat/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock
An Indian paramilitary soldier stands guard near the Ghanta Ghar (Clock Tower) in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir.Photograph: Firdous Nazir/NurPhoto/Shutterstock
Indian businessmen pray in front of their record-keeping books as part of a ritual to worship the Hindu wealth deity Goddess Lakshmi in Ahmedabad.Photograph: Amit Dave/Reuters

A Hindu devotee lights earthen lamps in Srinagar. Diwali is likely a fusion of harvest festivals in ancient India and is mentioned in early Sanskrit texts composed between the 7th and 10th centuries.Photograph: Farooq Khan/EPA
Devotees perform rituals while worshipping an idol of Goddess Kali at the Kali Puja festival during Diwali in Siliguri, West Bengal.Photograph: Diptendu Dutta/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

A drone formation depicting Lord Hanuman illuminates the night sky during Dilli Ki Diwali, organised by the Delhi government at Central Park, Connaught Place, New Delhi.Photograph: Adil Abass/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock
Participants perform a martial arts display on the eve of the Diwali and Kali Puja festivals in Kolkata.Photograph: Debarchan Chatterjee/NurPhoto/Shutterstock
